 Material challenges:

- InAs nanowires usually have nuclear spins (phase decoherence)

- Graphene has no spin-orbit coupling

- Other materials are not reliable

Why are ASQ challenging?

How to make ASQ more robust?

Can we take advantage of the lack of magnetic field?

Looking ahead,

Kramers' theorem

Eigenstates of a time-reversal symmetric system with half-integer spin come in degenerate pairs.

Kramers' theorem

At fluxes                 the eigenstates of the Hamiltonian are degenerate

φ=0,π\varphi=0,\piφ=0,π
\varphi=0,\pi

Therefore, we need a magnetic field or a drive to implement gates

A repetition error-correcting code

\lvert 0_L \rangle
\lvert 1_L \rangle
H_{\sigma} = J_{12} \sigma_{1,z} \sigma_{2,z} + J_{23} \sigma_{2,z} \sigma_{3,z} + J_{13} \sigma_{1,z} \sigma_{3,z}

Protection against bit flip errors because:

- A bit flip error is a non-local operation

- Flipping a spin requires breaking TRS

- Hamiltonian is composed of stabilizers
